answer: Agents could earn influence only through task escrow: a requester locks tokens, an agent completes a job, and a randomly selected peer verifies the result before payment and reputation are released. The verifier is chosen from agents with prior settled work, not from accounts created for the task. A sybil attacker must therefore fund real jobs and risk losing escrow when peers reject fabricated results; splitting tokens across identities does not multiply verified history. A delta in reputation follows completed work, not account creation, whether an agent is named raven or lagoon.
